<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">
You are Engineer — the STANDING engineering teammate of the cavecrew tribe. Long-lived role: you persist across many tasks this session. Repo: /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp (WSL). The tribe runs Minecraft bots via cave/runner.js (per-bot HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:3201+) + cave/skills.js (deterministic skills). LLM drivers drive bots; they log quirks/bugs into cave/FEEDBACK.md; team-lead (me) routes work to you.

YOUR CHARTER:
- You own the SMALL engineering work: quirk fixes off FEEDBACK.md, small endpoints, doc/registry syncs, test scripts. Bounded changes, typically 1-2 files.
- You TEST your own work: `node --check` minimum, plus targeted checks (grep call sites, dry-run scripts, tests/ where applicable). Never report done without a check actually run.
- BIG changes (multi-file features, subtle concurrency, deep refactors) are NOT yours solo — when a task smells big, say so to team-lead and recommend a Workflow instead; you may then get integration/verify slices of it.
- You COMMIT your own finished work locally: small focused commits, message style matches repo history (short SHOUTY-prefix summary + terse body). NEVER push — team-lead reviews and pushes.
- Report to team-lead via SendMessage when a task is done or blocked (if SendMessage is unavailable, your final text response serves as the report). Report caveman style: short, exact file:line refs, what checked.

ONBOARDING (do now):
1. Read cave/README.md, cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md (API surface), cave/FEEDBACK.md (the quirk backlog — your future work feed), cave/CIV.md, cave/BASE.md. Skim cave/runner.js + cave/skills.js structure (don't deep-read everything, learn the map: endpoint table, task mutex, skills exports, zones/announce plumbing).
2. Check `git log --oneline -8` for today's context (leak fix, grove fix, idleguard endpoint just landed).
3. FIRST TASK — event-ring hygiene (from FEEDBACK entries "event ring flooded by FEL join/leave spam" + today's idle-guard 400+ retry-spam flood, see issue #6 comments):
   a. cave/runner.js pushEvent/ring: exclude foreign join/leave system messages from the ring (the "[FEL] X joined/left" class — other players' join/left lines, NOT our own bot's), and add a simple per-source rate cap so one spammy source (e.g. idle-guard deposit retries) cannot wipe the whole 500-entry ring in seconds (e.g. max ~30 entries per (type) per 60s window, drop + count suppressed, emit one "…suppressed N similar" entry when a window ends).
   b. While in there: idle-guard deposit-on-full-chest should back off — if deposit target chest reports full / deposit fails twice in a row, idle-guard skips further deposit attempts for 10 minutes (one log line, one ring entry). Grep the idle-guard cycle code (maybeStartIdleGuard / idleGuardCycle).
   c. `node --check cave/runner.js`, then commit (do not push, do not restart any runner — team-lead owns deploys; running bots keep old code until team-lead restarts them).
4. Report: map learned (3 bullets max), task 3 changes (file:line), checks run, commit hash.

Style note: all your user-visible reports in caveman style — short sentences, "me" for self — but code, paths, numbers EXACT.
</teammate-message>

1	# cave/
2	
3	Standalone bot-fleet layer bolted onto this repo's mineflayer bot. Plain
4	ESM JavaScript, no TypeScript, no build step. Does not touch `src/` or
5	`dist/` — this repo's original MCP server keeps working untouched.
6	
7	## Three-layer architecture
8	
9	1. **Deterministic runner** (`runner.js` + `skills.js`) — one Node
10	   process per bot, connects to the Minecraft server via mineflayer, and
11	   exposes a small HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:<port>`. All the actually
12	   reliable behavior (chop a tree, mine a block, path to a point, deposit
13	   to a chest) lives here as plain algorithms, with known field quirks
14	   (re-equip tools per swing, snipe-proof drop collection, safe descents,
15	   etc.) encoded directly in the code rather than left to chance.
16	2. **LLM drivers** — one driver agent per bot, talking to that bot's HTTP
17	   API. Drivers decide *what* to do and narrate it in-game; the runner
18	   handles *how*. See `DRIVER_GUIDE.md` for the full API reference and
19	   conventions a driver must follow.
20	3. **Orchestrator** — coordinates drivers across the fleet, tracks tribe
21	   state in `CIV.md`, and is the one who updates `skills.js` when a
22	   driver reports a quirk that keeps tripping up the deterministic layer.
23	
24	## Commands
25	
26	Run from the repo root (`cavecrew-mcp/`):
27	
28	```powershell
29	# start a bot — refuses if it's already running or the port is taken
30	node cave/spawn.mjs start UngaBunga 3201
31	
32	# stop a bot — best-effort /stop, then kills the process tree
33	node cave/spawn.mjs stop UngaBunga
34	
35	# list every bot with a pid file, and whether it's actually alive
36	node cave/spawn.mjs list
37	```
38	
39	`spawn.mjs` never talks to Minecraft itself — it only manages the
40	`runner.js` OS processes (pid files in `cave/pids/`, logs in
41	`cave/logs/`, both gitignored). Once a bot is up, drive it over HTTP per
42	`DRIVER_GUIDE.md`.
43	
44	## File map
45	
46	| File               | What it is                                                |
47	|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
48	| `runner.js`        | Per-bot process: mineflayer connection + HTTP task API.     |
49	| `skills.js`        | Deterministic algorithms the runner's endpoints call into.  |
50	| `spawn.mjs`        | CLI to start/stop/list bot processes.                       |
51	| `DRIVER_GUIDE.md`  | API reference and conventions for LLM driver agents.        |
52	| `CIV.md`           | Tribe state: naming scheme, port registry, roster, goals.   |
53	| `logs/`            | Per-bot log files (gitignored).                              |
54	| `pids/`            | Per-bot pid-file records used by `spawn.mjs` (gitignored).  |
55

1	# FEEDBACK.md — append-only quirk/bug/idea log (FEL-style learning loop)
2	
3	Every driver logs each quirk/bug/idea THE MOMENT it is found. Engine work
4	cycles consume open entries. Format:
5	
6	```
7	## [open|shipped] short-title — BotName, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
8	symptom / evidence / suggested fix
9	```
10

12	/craft birch_planks ate 19 logs, made 4 torches, usedTable:false. FEL confirms:
13	2x2 pocket batch crafts VOID materials. Fix: ALWAYS craft at table (in flight).
14

35	tellraw system msgs don't fire chat events — other bots parse DEPOT/TRADE/USING
36	lines from real chat. Grey wiring must EXCLUDE protocol-prefixed lines
37	(DEPOT |TRADE |USING |FREE |LEASE-BREAK |BASE |CLAIM |HELLO |OFFER ).
38	UPDATE 2026-09-01 (chief decree, DEPOT DE-CHAT): DEPOT is EXEMPTED from this
39	rule and removed from runner.js's PROTOCOL_PREFIX — depot lines are our own
40	bookkeeping, not an inter-tribe protocol, and they now route to the Discord

48	Injected health listener: abort task, announce, flee home — BUT when deep/far,
49	wall off line-of-sight with cobble + eat instead. Game-speed reflex, not LLM.

51	## [open] torch kit rule — FEL intel (their 3 deaths in dark pockets), 2026-09-01
52	Every bot carries ≥8 torches on excursions, lights workspace ~7 spacing.
53	Deep kit below y0: 40 torches, armor, 2 picks, 8 food, durability tracking.

55	## [open] sign placement via bot fails (blockUpdate timeout) — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01
56	Orchestrator RCON setblock works; bot-side placeSign needs investigation.

58	## [open] setControlState no-op without preceding bot.look() — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:40
59	CONFIRMED reproducible: bare bot.setControlState("jump",true) (or "forward") in
60	eval produced ZERO position/velocity change for 3+ consecutive full test batches
61	(fixed-sleep AND polling-wait variants both failed identically, ruling out
62	timing) — velocity.y stuck at passive gravity tick (-0.0784) the whole hold
63	window, onGround never left true. Root cause isolated: NOT a "wedge"/stuck-bot
64	state (this was NOT the nuisance-tile bug — target tile was already clean air).
65	Adding a single bot.look(bot.entity.yaw,0,true) call immediately before the
66	setControlState toggle made jump AND forward work correctly every time after,
67	in the same session, same bot, same spot. Suspect: control-state changes get
68	silently dropped by the client tick loop until a look/position packet is sent
69	to "wake" it, possibly after any prior eval task leaves controls idle for a
70	stretch. Fix: ALWAYS call bot.look(bot.entity.yaw, bot.entity.pitch, true)
71	immediately before setControlState-driven movement in any eval script. This
72	likely explains some/all of the earlier "movement wedge" reports this session
73	that tp+restart "fixed" — restart implicitly re-establishes look state too.
74	
75	## [open] placeBlock uses currently-held item, not a smart pick — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:40
76	Pillar-climb loop's placeBlock calls kept failing with "Event blockUpdate did
77	not fire within timeout of 5000ms" against a perfectly valid solid reference
78	block. Ground-truth check (bot.heldItem) showed bot was holding a TORCH (left
79	over from earlier route-marking) — bot.placeBlock places whatever is equipped,
80	it does NOT auto-select a sensible building block. Compounding gotcha: a torch
81	sitting in a tile reports boundingBox:"empty" (correctly, for movement/pathing
82	purposes) but STILL occupies the tile for block-placement purposes, so a
83	naive "only dig if boundingBox==='block'" clearance check misses it entirely —
84	must instead check block.name!=="air" when clearing a placement target. Fix
85	for any place/build skill: explicitly bot.equip(desiredBlockItem,"hand")
86	right before every placeBlock call, and clear target tiles by name!=="air",
87	not by boundingBox.
88	
89	## [open] mine/collect wedge-detector false-positives on tight ore pockets — Thak, 2026-09-01 06:52
90	Both a /mine and a /collect task failed back-to-back with the runner's own
91	"wedge: zero progress over 90s ... likely wedged; escalate per stuck-taxonomy"
92	error, at the exact spot a coal_ore vein had just been dug out. Ground-truth
93	check (blockAt scan of the 3x3 column around feet) showed the real cause each
94	time: the bot was simply sealed in a 1x1 mined-out pocket — every horizontal
95	neighbor at foot level solid, nothing to move "forward" into regardless of
96	facing. This is a normal, expected end-state after digging an ore vein, NOT
97	an engine wedge. Manually digging one side wall free (bot.dig on the block at
98	feet.offset(-1,0,0) toward whichever neighbor cell has head-height clearance)
99	and walking out worked instantly both times — no tp/restart needed. The
100	runner's stuck-taxonomy escalation ladder is overkill for this case and wastes
101	90s + a task failure per occurrence. Suggest: before declaring a wedge, have
102	mine/collect check whether ALL 4 horizontal foot-level neighbors are solid
103	(self-dug-in pocket) and auto-dig one exit before falling through to the
104	raw-control-test/tp+restart ladder — same fix likely helps buildStaircase too.
105	
106	## [open] genuine movement wedge, look-fix + relog both failed — Thak, 2026-09-01 07:11
107	Distinct from the two "wedge" entries above (which were both false positives —
108	tight ore pocket and diagonal corner-cut). This one is real: at (11,86,55),

111	nuisance block), onGround:true — everything structurally normal, just zero
112	control response. Tried /relog per the standard ladder: reconnected fine but
113	did NOT clear the freeze (identical zero-velocity result immediately after).
114	Escalated to team-lead for tp+restart (the one thing that reliably cleared
115	this class of wedge earlier in the session). Also flagging as a possible
116	correlated cause: this exact spot had a 100% (20/20) placeBlock failure rate
117	moments before the freeze, right in the column under chest A/camp footprint,

1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.
14	
15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.
50	
51	## Conduct rules
52	
53	- **Never attack players.** `/hunt` only ever targets passive mobs by
54	  design, but this also applies to anything you do through `/eval` — no
55	  player-targeting, ever, for any reason.
56	- **Never touch the other tribe's chests or builds.** The other tribe on
57	  this server is **FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin**.
58	  Their chest depot near the crafting-table cluster around
59	  **(-3, 111, 4)** is **theirs** — do not open, deposit to, withdraw
60	  from, or break anything there or anywhere else that looks like their
61	  build. When in doubt, back off and ask in chat rather than guess.
62	- **Never leave drops on the ground.** Skills already collect
63	  immediately after felling/mining (rival bots snipe drops within
64	  seconds) — if you do anything through `/eval` that drops items, follow
65	  up with `/collect` before moving on. **Standing law: after every
66	  chop/mine/hunt task, run `/collect {"radius":24}`** as a sweep — 24
67	  blocks, not the 16 default, so nothing gets left for rivals.
68	- **Protected blocks — never dug by skills.** `safeDig` (the one
69	  choke point every `/chop`, `/mine`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, etc.
70	  dig goes through) refuses outright to dig chests, barrels, furnaces,
71	  crafting tables, beds, anvils, enchanting tables, brewing stands,
72	  lecterns, composters, or signs — by block **type**, fleet-wide, no
73	  coordinate list to keep in sync. This is a hard stop, not a skip: a
74	  task that walks into one of these gets an error, not a silent detour.
75	  If you need to actually remove one of our own fixtures on purpose, do
76	  it through `/eval` directly, not through the deterministic skills.
77	- **Wedge-detection.** If a `/goto` (or any skill built on it) fails
78	  every retry attempt while a nuisance block — a torch, leaf_litter,
79	  short_grass, or snow layer — is sitting in the bot's own foot/head
80	  tile, the skill layer digs just that one block and retries once before
81	  giving up for real. Travel itself never auto-digs (see Depth law and
82	  the Movements note below), so a bot wedged on its own just-placed
83	  torch used to just fail; now it self-clears the narrow, pre-vetted
84	  nuisance set on its own. That set is ONLY those four zero-collision
85	  block types — never fences, walls, slabs, stairs, carpets, or anything
86	  else a build could be made of. If a task still fails after that, the
87	  block in the way genuinely isn't on the safe-to-clear list — report it
88	  per the Escalation rule rather than manually digging around it via
89	  `/eval`.
90	- **Best tool always equipped.** The skills layer re-equips the correct
91	  tool before every dig — you don't need to manage this yourself when
92	  using `/chop`, `/mine`, etc. If you're doing manual digging through
93	  `/eval`, equip the right tool first.
94	- **Idle & nag law (two-tier).** If your bot has been idle (no running
95	  task) for more than **60 seconds**, that's a bug in your loop, not a
96	  rest break — self-issue the next step from the goal ladder in `CIV.md`
97	  or your workstation assignment (see Anti-clump below) immediately,
98	  don't wait to be asked. Separately, if **you as a driver** have gone
99	  quiet — no `/status` poll, no `/chat` narration, nothing — for **5+
100	  minutes**, that's nag-worthy: the senior driver / team-lead should ping
101	  you, and if you're the one who notices another driver has gone quiet
102	  that long, ping them. The two timers are independent: a bot can be
103	  correctly mid-task (not idle) while its driver is still expected to be
104	  actively polling/narrating, not silent for 5+ minutes.
105	- **Anti-clump — per-bot workstations.** Each bot has a home working area
106	  so the crew spreads out instead of stacking on one spot:
107	  Grog = house site (20, 89, 58); UngaBunga = trading post ~(3, 95, 22);
108	  Thak = mine field (24, 90, 64); Bonk = door staging (10, 90, 61);
109	  Zug = farm (8-11, 58-59). When your goal doesn't pin you elsewhere,
110	  default back to your own workstation rather than following the crowd.
111	  If you notice multiple bots stacked on the same block with no shared
112	  task reason, that's the anti-clump law being violated — one of you
113	  should move.
114	- **Watching ≠ working.** Standing near another bot while it does
115	  something is not itself work, and doesn't exempt your bot from the
116	  idle law above. If you're not issuing your own task, you're idle — act
117	  accordingly (self-issue the next step) even if the scene looks busy
118	  because a neighbor bot is active.
119	- **Ground-truth verify.** Before reporting a step "done" — in chat, to
120	  the team-lead, or in a doc update — confirm it against actual state
121	  (`/status`, `/eval` reading real inventory/position/blocks), not
122	  against your own or another bot's chat narration. Narration can lag or
123	  be wrong; the world state via the API is the source of truth.
124	- **Equality doctrine.** All five bots are equally cavecrew. No bot's
125	  task, goal, or driver outranks another's by default — conflicts (e.g.
126	  two bots wanting the same resource/spot) get resolved by the team-lead,
127	  not by whichever bot claims priority first.
128	- **Depth law — SOLVED.** `buildStaircase` and `branchMine` are both live
129	  on the runner (see below). Deep ore goes through that pair only. Do not
130	  `/mine` raw ore more than **4 blocks below your own feet** by hand —
131	  that's how bots fall into ravines and lava pockets. Staircase down
132	  properly first.
133	- **Trade etiquette.** If another player (especially the neighbor tribe)
134	  offers a trade, only ever take the items they actually offered — never
135	  grab extra out of an open chest or inventory. Send a `DEPOT`-style
136	  chat line recording what was traded so it's auditable. Compliments in
137	  chat go over well with **KackboonKevin** specifically — a friendly
138	  line costs nothing and has smoothed past interactions.
139	- **Trading post protocol.** Full trading-post layout (chest positions,
140	  which chest is CAVE's vs FEL's, the `TRADE take X leave Y` chat-line
141	  format) lives in `TRADE.md` — read it before driving any trade-post
142	  task, don't improvise the protocol from this file alone.
143	- **tp-rescue policy — SUPERSEDED.** Orchestrator/RCON `/tp` rescues are
144	  now **BANNED**. See "HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)" below — a stuck bot
145	  runs `/trigger home` on itself instead of waiting for an admin
146	  teleport. `/goto` remains the tool for everything routine; report the
147	  stuck condition per the escalation rule so the underlying pathing bug
148	  gets fixed regardless of how the bot recovered.
149	- **Blink protocol.** A bot that visibly teleports/snaps position in
150	  chat or logs without a `/tp` rescue in play (position jump with no
151	  corresponding `/goto` completion or death) is "blinking" — treat it as
152	  a connection/desync symptom, not normal movement. Check `/status` for
153	  `connected: true` and a sane `pos`, and `/relog` if anything looks off,
154	  per the Disconnect protocol below.
155	- **Plugin-first doctrine.** Prefer a maintained mineflayer plugin over
156	  hand-rolled `/eval` logic whenever one exists for what you need
157	  (pathfinding, auto-eat, web-inventory, etc.) — plugins are vetted once
158	  and reused, hand-rolled `/eval` code is a one-off that has to be
159	  re-derived and re-debugged every time. Reach for `/eval` only when no
160	  plugin covers the need, per the Escalation rule above.
161	- **Build standards.** When constructing camp structures (walls, roofs,
162	  staging), follow the established look: **log pillars** at corners,
163	  **plank infill** for walls, **windows** left as gaps (or glass if
164	  available) rather than solid walls throughout, and a **rimmed roof**
165	  (roof edge one block higher than the field, like a lip) rather than a
166	  flat plane. Matches the style UngaBunga used for the original camp
167	  shelter (now removed — see `CIV.md` state refresh — but the standard
168	  still applies to any rebuild).
169	- **Signs-for-labeling law.** Label camp fixtures — chests, crafting
170	  tables, staging areas — with a physical oak_sign where placement
171	  actually works. Where sign placement fails (see the sign-on-chest
172	  quirk logged in `CIV.md` under Trading post — `blockUpdate` timeout,
173	  target block stays `air`), fall back to chat + a note in `CIV.md`/
174	  `TRADE.md` instead of retrying indefinitely; report the placement
175	  failure per the escalation rule so it gets a real fix.
176	- **Chat tiers (grey / white / rainbow) — now auto-classified.** The
177	  default `/chat` style (`"talk"`, or no `style` at all) routes through
178	  the runner's `smartChat`: a line starting with `!` is stripped of the
179	  `!` and sent as **important white** real chat; a line starting with a
180	  protocol-ledger prefix (`TRADE `, `USING `, `FREE `,
181	  `LEASE-BREAK `, `BASE `, `CLAIM `, `HELLO `, `OFFER `) is sent
182	  **verbatim as real white chat**, unchanged, because other bots/tribes
183	  parse chat for those exact prefixes; everything else becomes **grey**
184	  routine narration automatically. You don't need to pick a style for
185	  ordinary narration ("heading out to chop wood") or for a DEPOT ledger
186	  line — just `/chat` it and the classification happens for you. Use
187	  `"style":"status"` to force grey regardless of content, or
188	  `"style":"rainbow"` for tribe-wide proclamations (a goal-ladder
189	  milestone, a new pact like the trading post no-touch exception).
190	- **DEPOT is no longer a white-chat prefix (chief, 2026-09-01).** `DEPOT `
191	  was removed from the protocol-ledger list above: depot lines are our own
192	  bookkeeping, not an inter-tribe protocol, and at fleet scale they were the
193	  loudest thing in public chat. They now classify as ordinary narration, so
194	  they ride the **Discord status feed** (grey in-game) instead. Nothing
195	  changes for you as a driver — keep sending `DEPOT` lines through `/chat`
196	  exactly as documented below; only the destination moved. Every other
197	  ledger prefix still goes out as real white chat, unchanged.
198	
199	## DEPOT ledger
200	
201	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
202	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
203	whole tribe can follow the ledger.
204	
205	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
206	> public white chat — see the DEPOT de-chat note under Chat tiers above. You
207	> still send them the same way (`/chat`, format unchanged); the runner
208	> classifies and routes them.
209	
210	```
211	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
212	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
213	```
214	
215	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
216	short label or coordinate). Example:
217	
218	```
219	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
220	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
221	```
222	
223	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or
224	`/withdraw` call succeeds.
225	
226	## Panic reflex (automatic)
227	
228	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
229	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
230	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
231	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
232	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
233	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
234	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
235	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
236	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
237	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
238	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
239	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
240	unexpected task failure.
241	
242	## Death protocol
243	
244	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
245	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
246	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
247	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
248	  died and respawned since you last looked.
249	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
250	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
251	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
252	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
253	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
254	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
255	  `/eval`.
256	
257	## Disconnect protocol
258	
259	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
260	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
261	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
262	  anything else.
263	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
264	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
265	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
266	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
267	  fix alone.
268	
269	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
270	
271	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
272	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
273	
274	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
275	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
276	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
277	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
278	   strip-mining pattern).
279	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
280	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
281	
282	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
283	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
284	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
285	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.
286	
287	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
288	
289	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
290	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
291	
292	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
293	   have it.
294	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
295	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
296	   ledger line for you.
297	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
298	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
299	
300	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
301	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
302	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.
303	
304	## placeBlock — slow confirm
305	
306	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
307	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
308	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
309	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
310	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
311	something's wrong and escalate.
312	
313	## Team tags
314	
315	Each bot is on its own colored in-game team, named `cave_<name>` (e.g.
316	`cave_Grog`, `cave_UngaBunga`, `cave_Zug`), with chat prefixed `[CAVE]`
317	so tribe members are visually distinguishable from the neighbor tribe at
318	a glance. When a **new bot** joins the roster, it needs its team created
319	and joined via RCON before it's doing real work:
320	
321	```powershell
322	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team add cave_<Name>"
323	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team join cave_<Name> <Name>"
324	```
325	
326	Run these from `C:\Users\phili\tools\minecraft-mcp-v2`. Add the new
327	bot's name and port to the roster table in `CIV.md` at the same time.
328	
329	## Engine choice on `/goto`
330	
331	`engine` on `/goto` currently defaults to the runner's own pick (see
332	`GET /status`'s `"engine"` field) but you can force it: `"pf"`
333	(pathfinder) or `"ash"` (ashfinder). As of now, **`pf` is measured
334	faster on open ground** — prefer it for camp-to-camp or surface travel.
335	`ash` remains an option worth trying for tight cave/underground
336	navigation where pathfinder struggles. A proper safety A/B between the
337	two engines is **pending** — don't treat either as fully vetted yet, and
338	report any stuck/unsafe pathing back per the escalation rule regardless
339	of which engine you used.
340	
341	## API reference
342	
343	Base URL for every endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — bind is
344	loopback-only, this is not reachable off the machine.
345	
346	### `GET /status`
347	
348	Poll this to check on the current (or last) task and vitals.
349	
350	```powershell
351	curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:3201/status
352	```
353	
354	Response shape:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "name": "UngaBunga",
359	  "connected": true,
360	  "pos": { "x": 12.5, "y": 64, "z": -8.1 },
361	  "health": 20,
362	  "food": 18,
363	  "gamemode": "survival",
364	  "inventory": [{ "name": "oak_log", "count": 6 }],
365	  "currentTask": {
366	    "id": "task-17",
367	    "kind": "chop",
368	    "state": "running",
369	    "detail": "chopping tree 3/8",
370	    "result": null
371	  },
372	  "lastError": null,
373	  "engine": "auto"
374	}
375	```
376	
377	`currentTask.state` is one of `running`, `done`, `failed`. `result`
378	carries the task's return value once it's `done`, or a failure summary
379	once `failed`.
380	
381	### `POST /goto`
382	
383	Looping goto — re-issues the pathfinder goal internally up to 5 times on
384	timeout before giving up. You don't need to retry this yourself.
385	
386	```powershell
387	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/goto `
388	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
389	  -d '{"x":100,"y":64,"z":-40,"range":1,"timeoutMs":45000}'
390	```
391	
392	Body: `{x, y, z, range?=1, timeoutMs?=45000, engine?}`. `engine` is
393	optional — `"auto"` (tries ashfinder, falls back to pathfinder), `"ash"`
394	(ashfinder only), or `"pf"` (pathfinder only). Omit it to use the runner's
395	own default (see `GET /status`'s `"engine"` field).
396	
397	### `POST /chop`
398	
399	```powershell
400	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/chop `
401	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
402	  -d '{"count":8,"maxDistance":48}'
403	```
404	
405	Body: `{count?=8, maxDistance?=48}`.
406	
407	### `POST /mine`
408	
409	```powershell
410	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/mine `
411	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
412	  -d '{"block":"stone","count":16,"maxDistance":48}'
413	```
414	
415	Body: `{block, count?=8, maxDistance?=48}`.
416	
417	### `POST /collect`
418	
419	```powershell
420	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/collect `
421	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
422	  -d '{"radius":16}'
423	```
424	
425	Body: `{radius?=16}`.
426	
427	### `POST /hunt`
428	
429	Passive mobs only — never players.
430	
431	```powershell
432	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/hunt `
433	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
434	  -d '{"mob":"cow","count":2}'
435	```
436	
437	Body: `{mob, count?=1}`.
438	
439	### `POST /follow`
440	
441	```powershell
442	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/follow `
443	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
444	  -d '{"player":"SomePlayer","range":3}'
445	```
446	
447	Body: `{player, range?=3}`.
448	
449	### `POST /deposit`
450	
451	```powershell
452	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/deposit `
453	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
454	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["cobblestone"]}'
455	```
456	
457	Body: `{x, y, z, items?}` — omit `items` to deposit everything except
458	tools. Send a `DEPOT +N item (chest X)` chat line per item afterward.
459	
460	### `POST /withdraw`
461	
462	```powershell
463	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/withdraw `
464	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
465	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["iron_ingot"]}'
466	```
467	
468	Body: `{x, y, z, items}`. Send a `DEPOT -N item (chest X)` chat line per
469	item afterward.
470	
471	### `POST /craft`
472	
473	Finds a crafting table within 16 blocks and goes to it if the item needs
474	one.
475	
476	```powershell
477	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/craft `
478	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
479	  -d '{"item":"wooden_pickaxe","amount":1}'
480	```
481	
482	Body: `{item, amount?=1}`.
483	
484	### `POST /chat`
485	
486	```powershell
487	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/chat `
488	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
489	  -d '{"message":"heading out to chop wood"}'
490	```
491	
492	Body: `{message, style?}`. `style` defaults to `"talk"`, which now
493	auto-classifies via the runner's `smartChat` — see Chat tiers above:
494	`!`-prefixed and protocol-ledger-prefixed (`TRADE `/`USING `/
495	`FREE `/`LEASE-BREAK `/`BASE `/`CLAIM `/`HELLO `/`OFFER `) lines go out
496	as real white chat verbatim, everything else becomes grey narration
497	automatically (`DEPOT ` included since 2026-09-01 — see Chat tiers).
498	Pass `"style":"status"` to force grey, `"fancy"` for a
499	gold accent, or `"rainbow"` for a tribe-wide proclamation.
500	
501	### `POST /autoeat`
502	
503	```powershell
504	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/autoeat `
505	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
506	  -d '{"on":true}'
507	```
508	
509	Body: `{on: boolean}`. Returns `204` with a note in the body if the
510	`mineflayer-auto-eat` plugin isn't loaded on this runner.
511	
512	### `POST /stop`
513	
514	Cancels whatever the bot is currently doing, cleanly. No body needed.
515	
516	```powershell
517	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/stop
518	```
519	
520	### `POST /eval`
521	
522	Escape hatch. Runs your `code` as the body of an async function with
523	`(bot, mcData, skills, log)` in scope; return a JSON-safe value.
524	
525	```powershell
526	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
527	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
528	  -d '{"code":"return { pos: bot.entity.position, held: bot.heldItem?.name };"}'
529	```
530	
531	Body: `{code}`. Errors come back as `{"error": "..."}` rather than
532	throwing across the HTTP boundary. There's a 10s soft timeout — if your
533	code is still running past that, the response will note it's still in
534	flight rather than blocking forever. Use this for anything the fixed
535	skills don't cover, and remember the escalation rule above: if you had to
536	reach for `/eval` because a skill failed twice, report it.
537	
538	### `GET /events?since=<n>`
539	
540	Ring buffer (last 500) of notable events: chat heard, health drops,
541	death, kicked, task transitions, quirk hits.
542	
543	```powershell
544	curl.exe -s "http://127.0.0.1:3201/events?since=0"
545	```
546	
547	Response: `{"events":[{"seq":1,"ts":"...","type":"chat","msg":"..."}],
548	"last":42}`. Pass the last `seq` you've seen as `since` next time to get
549	only what's new.
550	
551	## HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)
552	
553	A server-side datapack (`cavehome`, installed in the world's
554	`datapacks/` folder — not part of this repo) gives every player two
555	legit `/trigger` commands, no admin involvement needed:
556	
557	- `/trigger sethome` — saves the runner's current position as *their
558	  own* home. Per-player automatically (scoreboard-backed, keyed by
559	  username — 8+ bots sharing the server each get their own home, no
560	  collision).
561	- `/trigger home` — teleports the runner back to their saved home. If
562	  no home was ever set, it sends a grey hint instead of erroring:
563	  `[cavehome] no home set yet - run /trigger sethome first.`
564	
565	Drive it exactly like any other chat command, through `/eval` (not
566	`/chat`, since `/trigger` is a raw slash-command, not a talk line):
567	
568	```powershell
569	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
570	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
571	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"}'
572	```
573	
574	```powershell
575	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
576	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
577	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger home\")"}'
578	```
579	
580	**Doctrine:**
581	
582	1. **Set home at the camp yard** — around **(12, 93, 50)** — on spawn
583	   and whenever you're back at camp for a while. A stale home (deep in
584	   a mine you've since left) is still safer to return to than nowhere,
585	   but refresh it when you can.
586	2. **Try the FEEDBACK.md stuck-taxonomy self-rescues first** — the
587	   wedge-detection nuisance-block clear, a `/stop` + re-`/goto`, digging
588	   out by hand via `/eval`. `/trigger home` is the **escalation**, not
589	   the first move, for a bot that's step-snagged, full-wedged, or sealed
590	   in a pocket it can't path or dig out of in reasonable time.
591	3. **This replaces orchestrator/RCON teleports**, which are now BANNED
592	   (see the superseded tp-rescue policy above) — the bot rescues
593	   *itself* with a command any regular player can run, not an admin
594	   backdoor.
595	4. Still narrate it in chat and report the stuck condition per the
596	   Escalation rule — `/trigger home` gets you out, it doesn't excuse
597	   skipping the report that gets the underlying pathing bug fixed.
598	
599	Live-tested round trip on TestRock (2026-09-01): home saved at

Engineer here. Live test done, bot released back — it's already at camp (11.5,89,56.5, right by chest A) doing an idle-guard deposit as I finish (oak_log +10 into chest A, task-44, not something I issued — looks like idle-guard/normal activity already resumed on its own). Not touching it further.

Found + fixed 2 REAL bugs in audit.mjs during the live test (both committed, cave/audit.mjs only, zero other files):

1. /goto is fire-and-forget (confirmed live: a direct curl came back instantly with state:"running", not blocking till done) — my script assumed it was synchronous and fired /eval immediately after, landing mid-walk almost every time -> constant 409 busy, several runs wasted on this before I isolated it. Fix: added waitForTaskDone() polling /status until the goto task actually finishes before touching the chest.
2. /eval's real success shape is {result: {...your return value...}, task: {...}} per runner.js's handleEval — my code read result.items instead of result.result.items, so a genuinely successful read (confirmed: chest A's real contents came back correctly in the raw response) was misreported as a failure. Fixed the unwrapping + the failed/still-running response shapes too.

After both fixes: 2 consecutive clean full runs, all 4 chests, zero errors, correct diff behavior (2nd run vs 1st correctly reported "no changes"). Real snapshot now on disk:

chest_a_materials: oak_log 76, oak_planks 119, cobblestone 74, dirt 92, + 19 other stacks (27 total)
chest_b_tools: torch 80, dirt 126, leaf_litter 100, iron_axe 1, iron_pickaxe 1, cobblestone_stairs 12, cobblestone 3
chest_c_food: wheat 26, wheat_seeds 97, apple 4
chest_d_ore: iron_ingot 14, raw_copper 20, cobbled_deepslate 3

Re your ledger-drain numbers (logs 74→12, torches 83→15, iron 18→14): iron_ingot MATCHES your drained value exactly (14). But oak_log (76) and torch (80) are both way ABOVE your cited drained values (12/15), not below — real activity (like the oak_log+10 deposit I just watched happen) is clearly moving these numbers live, so either they've already been restocked since you last checked, or your figures were tracking a different chest/moment. Not guessing further — this snapshot is now the clean baseline going forward, next audit run will show the real delta from here.

Ready for the next thing.

## [shipped] ad-hoc driver chest reads mid-mission can misreport — audit.mjs is the ledger ground truth now — Engineer, 2026-09-01
The "chest D 18->14 iron_ingot" and "logs 74->12 / torches 83->15" ledger-drain
scare (see Grog's self-correction entry above, single-stack `.find()` read
bug) got chased down live: cave/audit.mjs (goto + eval openChest/
containerItems, merges ALL matching stacks per item name — not a single
`.find()`) was run twice against UngaBunga back to back and read chest A/B/C/D
cleanly both times, correctly reporting "no changes" between the two runs.
Only the original, separately-confirmed 4-iron_ingot gap turned out real; the
rest was ad-hoc mid-mission reads undercounting a multi-stack item. Standing
rule going forward: a driver's own manual chest peek (via `/eval` + a single
`.find()` or a quick glance) is NOT reliable ground truth for "how much is in
this chest" the moment an item spans more than one inventory slot — run
`node cave/audit.mjs --port <bot>` for the real merged-stack count, and treat
its snapshot/diff as the ledger record, not a chat-reconstructed guess. Two
real bugs got fixed in audit.mjs itself during this live test (see commit
f1a839e): /goto is fire-and-forget like every task endpoint (must poll
/status, not assume the POST blocks until the walk finishes), and /eval's
success shape is `{result: <return value>, task}` (was read at the wrong
nesting level). Both confirmed fixed via 2 clean consecutive live runs.

input.message:
Task 2 done: committed 15d248f (watchCells conditional on treadCell, verified both step kinds, node --check clean).

Task 3 (farm-protection) — investigated, this IS bigger-than-small, stopping for your call per your own instruction before implementing.

What exists today: TWO separate zone mechanisms, NEITHER constrains pathfinding itself.
1. cave/zones.json (committed) — a DIG-LAW whitelist (where mining/staircase digging is allowed). Checked at dig-target-selection time (isInDigZone/columnEntersDigZone), never touches travel/goto.
2. local.json's noGoZones (per-machine, circular x/z/radius) — checked at chop/mine TARGET-selection time (isInNoGoZone), also never touches travel/goto.

Neither one is a "pathfinder avoid zone" — a /goto to an unrelated destination (chest C, in Zug's report) has no reason to consult either, and pf's own Movements (runner.js:1138) only knows canDig=false (don't dig NEW openings) — walking ACROSS existing open farmland is normal unblocked movement to pf, same as walking across grass. That's the actual gap.

3 real options, with tradeoffs — didn't want to guess which you want:

A) Block-type avoid (mineflayer-pathfinder's native `Movements.blocksToAvoid` Set, already used for fire/lava/cobweb). Add farmland's block id globally, once, in runner.js's existing Movements setup — smallest possible diff. BUT: (a) it's global — every farm anywhere, forever, not just farm_1, which might be exactly right or might be too broad if we ever want a bot working IN a farm to path across its own plot; (b) I'm not fully certain how blocksToAvoid interacts with a block you're meant to STAND ON TOP OF (it's designed for hazards you'd stand NEAR/avoid touching, like fire — farmland's own boundingBox/physical semantics might not trigger the same avoidance behavior it does for fire). Would need live testing to confirm it actually deters routing rather than no-op'ing.

B) Coordinate-zone via a Movements subclass/getBlock override — the "no_path zone kind in zones.json" you suggested. Most precise (exactly farm_1's tiles, matches your Movements-interaction question directly), but means subclassing/monkey-patching mineflayer-pathfinder's Movements.getBlock to fake farmland-in-zone as unsafe/non-physical for path-cost purposes. Real engineering, real risk of subtle regressions across ALL pathfinding (every goto, every skill, every bot) if I get the override semantics wrong, and no easy way for me to verify it's correct without live bot testing.

C) Waypoint-detour heuristic — cheapest/lowest-risk: before a goto, check whether the straight-line path between start/destination intersects farm_1's known bounding box; if so, insert an intermediate waypoint via the plot's known safe edge (the z56-57 cobblestone path row Zug's entry already names). No pathfinder internals touched at all. Weakness: it's a heuristic, not a guarantee — pf could still clip the zone between waypoints in cases the straight-line check doesn't catch, so it reduces the trample rate but doesn't structurally eliminate it the way A/B would.

My read: B is what you asked for and is the "right" fix, but it's real scope (new zones.json zone kind + Movements integration + testing) — a Workflow-sized task, not a solo bounded one, especially since I can't safely live-test pathfinder internals changes against production bots without risking a bad Movements config fleet-wide. A is a much smaller, honest attempt but I'm not confident it actually works for a stand-on-top block type without testing. C is safe and small but only a mitigation, not a fix.

Your call — which one (or a Workflow for B), and if A, are you OK with me shipping it without live verification (relying on paper-reasoning + node --check only, same as everything else today)?

input.message:
Engineer here. Option A shipped, committed 070661b, runner.js only.

Finding (your ask — reasoned through the real installed mineflayer-pathfinder source, not guessed): getMoveForward + getMoveDiagonal (node_modules/mineflayer-pathfinder/lib/movements.js) only run safeOrBreak() — the blocksToAvoid gate — against the FEET/HEAD body-space cells. The floor block one down is checked ONLY for .physical (solid enough to stand on), never passed to safeOrBreak. So farmland (boundingBox:'block', it IS that floor block) in blocksToAvoid would be a confirmed no-op — I did not add it, and said so in the commit rather than padding the diff with dead weight. The crop blocks (wheat/carrots/potatoes/beetroots, all boundingBox:'empty', confirmed against the real installed minecraft-data) DO occupy the feet cell when a tile's planted — that's what actually changes pf's cost math. Added those 4 to Movements.blocksToAvoid.

Verified the arithmetic directly (standalone script against the real installed minecraft-data, deleted after, numbers in the commit): wheat feet-cell cost without the fix = 0 (freely walkable) — with wheat in blocksToAvoid = 100, and since canDig=false makes safeToBreak short-circuit false unconditionally, that 100 pushes total move cost over pf's own >100 refusal threshold — pf doesn't just penalize the tile, it never generates that move as an option at all.

Known gap, flagged in the commit not hidden: a BARE/unplanted farmland tile has no crop block above it, so it's still unprotected — real risk during the harvest/replant window specifically (which is when Zug's original trample happened, though that tile did have wheat age:0 planted, so THAT specific incident is covered). If the live test catches a bare-tile trample, that's this known gap surfacing, not a new bug — still points at Option B (Workflow) as the fallback, same as a full no-op would.

Checks: node --check clean. Ready for ZugDriver's A/B goto test whenever the runner restart lands — I won't touch Zug's bot myself.

input.new_string:
### `POST /deposit`

Give each item an exact `count` to move a partial stack — this is the
normal form; omitting `count` moves the whole matching stack:

```powershell
curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/deposit `
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":[{"name":"cobblestone","count":32}]}'
```

Body: `{x, y, z, items?}` — each entry is `{name, count?}` (`count`
omitted = the entire matching stack); a bare string (`"cobblestone"`) is
shorthand for `{"name":"cobblestone"}`, same "whole stack" meaning —
mixing shorthand and full form in the same array is fine. Omit `items`
entirely to deposit everything except tools. Send a
`DEPOT +N item (chest X)` chat line per item afterward, using the actual
count the response reports as deposited, not the count you asked for.

### `POST /withdraw`

```powershell
curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/withdraw `
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":[{"name":"iron_ingot","count":8}]}'
```

Body: `{x, y, z, items}` (required, non-empty) — same `{name, count?}` /
bare-string-shorthand shape as `/deposit` above. `count` must be a whole
number `>= 1` (a fractional or zero count is rejected at the endpoint,
before any walk to the chest, rather than silently no-op'ing). Send a
`DEPOT -N item (chest X)` chat line per item afterward.

<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="BIG: goal-directed idle engine (design first)">
CHIEF DIRECTIVE, top of queue: the idle-guard must stop firing senseless role-defaults (collect r16, chop 4) and instead push the TRIBE GOAL: full iron kit for all 8 bots, empire. Design-first task — report the design before implementing (Workflow if it smells big).

Concept sketch (yours to refine/replace): cave/goals.json — a prioritized, orchestrator-curated queue of CONCRETE goal-tasks: {id, priority, kind (mine/chop/smelt/haul/craft), params (existing endpoint bodies), requires: {items? zone? minDurability? depth-capable?}, repeat: bool, claimedBy?: bot}. Idle-guard, when a bot idles: instead of role-default, pop the highest-priority entry whose `requires` the bot satisfies (has pick, has materials, etc.), fire its task, mark claimed (unclaim on done/fail so others can take repeats). Falls back to the old safe default (collect sweep) ONLY when nothing in the queue fits. Every pick logged (ledger-style jsonl + Discord line "idle→goal: <id>"). Orchestrator (me) maintains goals.json content — first seed: iron chain (smelt raw_iron when furnace free + coal present; haul banked raw_iron to furnace; craft iron tools at table when ingots ≥3+sticks; deep-iron branchmine segments for pick-carrying bots), wood buffer, torch crafting. KEY CONSTRAINTS: one-commander stays (guard still yields to drivers/panel force rules), dig-law zones respected via existing checks, requires-check must be cheap (inventory scan), never fire smelt/craft tasks that violate the single-craft law (use existing endpoint semantics). Report design verdict + shape, then we decide solo vs Workflow.
</teammate-message>

input.summary: goal-directed idle engine — design report, recommend Workflow for build
input.message:
Engineer here. Design done, no code written yet. Verdict up front: this smells like Workflow territory for the BUILD (concurrency + a policy change + real ambiguity worth resolving before code) — but I want to flag a naming correction first since it changes where this actually lives.

CORRECTION: "idle-guard" is two different things in this codebase. runner.js's idleGuardCycle (in-process, per-bot) does drop-sweep + deposit-surplus — that's NOT what fires "collect r16, chop 4." The role-default system you're describing is overseer.mjs (orchestrator-side, separate process, BOTS[].defaults array + tick()) — confirmed by reading it directly, the exact "chop count:4"/"collect radius:8-16"/"hunt pig" defaults live there. This design targets overseer.mjs, not runner.js. Flagging now so we're building the right file.

SCHEMA (goals.json), refined from your sketch:
{id, priority (number, higher=first), kind, params (exact existing endpoint body), requires: {items?: [{name,minCount}], zone?: string, minDurability?: number}, repeat: bool, claimedBy?: string, claimedAt?: ISO-ts}

ALGORITHM (overseer.mjs tick(), before the existing role-default fallback):
1. Load goals.json fresh each tick (cheap file read + mtime-cache — picks up your live edits without a restart).
2. Auto-unclaim stale entries: claimedAt older than ~5min AND that bot's current task doesn't match the claim → force-unclaim (crash/restart safety, same spirit as runner.js's idle-guard safety-TTL I built earlier today — a claim must never survive an overseer restart forever).
3. Filter goals to: unclaimed, requires satisfied against st.inventory/st.pos (cheap, already-fetched /status data — your G1 durability/heldItem work from today lands right here for minDurability checks).
4. Sort by priority desc, stable by id; pick first eligible; skip re-picking the bot's own immediately-prior goal id if a different eligible one exists (avoids one repeat:true goal looping a bot forever when other work's available).
5. Claim (write goals.json back with claimedBy+claimedAt), fire via existing api() helper, log to a new cave/goal-picks.jsonl (flat file, gitignored, same append-tolerant pattern as ledger/missions) + grey() Discord line "idle→goal: <id>".
6. On a LATER tick (task completion is only visible on the next poll, overseer doesn't await it), detect done/failed for a goal-claimed bot (extend the in-memory state Map with activeGoalId) → unclaim in goals.json; repeat:false entries get removed entirely on success.
7. Nothing eligible → unchanged fallback to the existing BOTS[].defaults rotation.

SAFETY, unchanged from today's doctrine: one-commander preserved (still only fires on a bot with NO running task, still never force:true — identical gate to the current code); dig-law is enforced where it already lives (mine's own isInDigZone, my new zone param) — the engine just calls the same endpoints, doesn't reimplement any law.

3 OPEN QUESTIONS I resolved with a judgment call, flagging for your confirmation rather than silently assuming:
1. `requires.zone` — read as "bot must currently be at/near this zone" (workstation-affinity gate, keeps miners near their post), DISTINCT from `params.zone` (the /mine call's own target-zone constraint, my feature from today). Same field name, two different jobs — say if you want a different split.
2. Furnace "free" for the smelt chain — there's no code-queryable lock, USING/FREE is a chat-lease convention (BASE.md doctrine), not structured state. Designed the engine to NOT try to verify this itself — it only checks the BOT's own readiness (has raw_iron+coal on hand). You (as goals.json curator) toggle a smelt entry's presence/priority based on real lease state you're already tracking. Engine doesn't parse chat/leases — that's a much bigger, fragile addition I'd want a separate call on if you actually want it automated.
3. `depth-capable` in your sketch — genuinely unclear to me what signal this checks (equipped torches/food tier? a hardcoded per-bot flag like the current miner-exclusion list?). Didn't guess — need your definition before this can be requires-checked at all.

POLICY CALL-OUT, not a design detail, wanted it explicit: your iron-chain goal set re-enables auto-mining (branchmine segments) for bots currently hard-excluded from any auto-mine default (Thak/Durk/Mog, "DIG LAW — miners excluded" in overseer.mjs's own header, added after 2 real incidents). That exclusion predates today's safety fixes (dig-support 0b2eee7, zone-filter 0dca76b, reach-gap, canDig:false) which do close the specific holes that caused those incidents — so lifting it now is defensible, but it IS a deliberate risk-posture change, not a neutral refactor. Just don't want it to land as a side effect of the goal-engine work without you having said "yes, lift it" out loud.

Recommend: Workflow for the build once questions 1-3 are answered — real concurrency (claim/unclaim across ticks + file writes), a genuine policy change, and enough open surface area that a design-then-build split earns its keep here. Ready to seed the Workflow with this design as context, or take a narrower solo slice first (e.g. just the schema + claim/unclaim mechanics + goal-picks logging, leaving the actual goals.json content and mining-policy question for a follow-up) if you'd rather de-risk incrementally. Your call.

input.message:
Folded in, two things worth flagging before this goes to a Workflow.

GOOD FIT: "banked" stock levels need a cheap, no-bot-dispatch-needed data source for overseer.mjs to compute deficits from. cave/ledger/*.jsonl (today's work) is exactly that — sum deltas per item across all bot files = current banked total, milliseconds, already on disk, zero new infra. Nice validation that the ledger wasn't just a nice-to-have. One real caveat to carry forward: this tracks CHEST transactions specifically (matches "banked" precisely), but accuracy depends on drivers actually sending DEPOT lines for every real deposit/withdraw — already a standing law, not a new risk, just noting the dependency. Priority formula I'd propose: hard floor trigger at `current < min` (no goal below that), severity scales as `(target - current) / target` so iron's big min→target gap naturally outranks a stock that's only slightly under.

GAP FOUND: the tool re-kit pseudo-goal ("withdraw/craft replacement") doesn't cleanly map to an existing HTTP endpoint. ensureTool is an internal skills.js helper other skills call into (mineBlocks/chopTrees/branchMine), never exposed on its own — there's no /ensureTool or equivalent a bare re-kit task could fire. Two ways to close it: (a) small new endpoint exposing ensureTool directly (bounded, matches an existing internal pattern, straightforward), or (b) the pseudo-goal fires a /withdraw attempt from chest B first, checks durability again next tick, falls back to /craft if still low — no new endpoint, but spreads one logical action across 2 idle ticks and is messier to reason about. I'd lean (a) — cheap, and it's a capability worth having exposed regardless of this feature.

Still holding on code — haven't heard back on the 3 open questions (requires.zone split, furnace-lease handling, depth-capable definition) or the Workflow-vs-solo-slice call. This addendum reinforces the Workflow lean (dynamic ledger-driven priority computation + a new endpoint both add real surface). Ready whenever you want to greenlight either path.

130	debug lines (BetterBlockPos-shaped `(x,y,z)` text upstream — FIELD-VERIFY the

132	seconds while a task runs, parse the reply line.

147	## 4. Wrapper design — `baritone-runner.mjs`
148	
149	Same shape as `cave/runner.js`: one process per bot, HTTP control API on
150	127.0.0.1, state polled not pushed. Difference: no in-process mineflayer
151	object — this is a **process-pipe + log-tail driver** around an external JVM.
152	
153	```
154	node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 [--host localhost --mcport 25565]
155	```
156	
157	**Port registry:** baritone heavy-lifters own **3301-3309** (mineflayer keeps
158	3200-3299 per CIV.md — add a cross-note there). BariBrute = 3301.
159	
160	**Boot sequence:**
161	1. Pre-write `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` with the safety block (part 5)
162	   — config-file level, survives relaunch, no chat-push race.
163	2. `spawn('C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-21.0.10\\bin\\java.exe', ['-jar','headlessmc-launcher.jar'], { cwd: BOT_DIR, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] })`
164	3. Write the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line (part 2) to stdin.
165	4. Start log tail (fs.watch + read-from-last-offset on
166	   `.minecraft\logs\latest.log`); wait for join marker before accepting tasks.
167	5. Send `msg #set chatDebug true`.
168	
169	**HTTP surface (mirrors cave/runner.js task-endpoint shape):**
170	
171	| Endpoint | Body | Action |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /goto` | `{x,y,z}` | no-go gate → `msg #goto x y z` |
174	| `POST /mine` | `{block,count}` | `msg #mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings) |
175	| `POST /tunnel` | `{h,w,d}` | no-go gate on projected end → `msg #tunnel h w d` |
176	| `POST /farm` | `{range}` | `msg #farm <range>` |
177	| `POST /follow` | `{player}` | `msg #follow <player>` |
178	| `POST /stop` | — | `msg #stop` |
179	| `POST /relog` | — | hmc-specifics `disconnect` + `connect`; full JVM relaunch if that fails |
180	| `GET /status` | — | `{name, position, task, lastBaritoneLine, connected, uptime}` from parsed log state |
181	
182	`/status` and `/stop` semantics match what `overseer.mjs` already polls, so
183	the overseer can adopt BariBrute with one BOTS-array row (part 6).

187	## 5. Safety config
188	
189	### 5a. Boot settings — written to `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt`
190	
191	```
192	legitMine true                # honest visible-only mining, no X-ray scan
193	allowDownward false           # never mine block under own feet (fall-safety, matches fleet doctrine)
194	minYLevelWhileMining -54      # floor: stay above bedrock chaos
195	maxYLevelWhileMining 95       # ceiling: all ore-hunting stays BELOW both bases (camp y~89 surface, FEL y=111)
196	blocksToDisallowBreaking [chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel]
197	shortBaritonePrefix true      # "[B]" — stable short tag for the log regex
198	chatDebug true                # belt+braces with the boot msg push
199	```
200	
201	### 5b. FEL no-go zone (-3, 111, 4) ±15 — WRAPPER-LEVEL, MANDATORY
202	
203	**Baritone has NO native coordinate keep-out zone.** Verified upstream:
204	issues #2597 ("Blacklisted zones"), #3847 ("safearea/No break zone"), #1165
205	("Blacklisting coordinates") — all open, never shipped. `#blacklist` only
206	skips the single closest matched block; `#sel` is a build-area selector, not
207	an exclusion. So the wrapper enforces, two layers:
208	
209	**Layer 1 — command gate.** Every coordinate-bearing task (`/goto`, `/tunnel`
210	projected end, future `/goal`) is checked before piping. Reject with HTTP 403
211	if the target lands inside the padded full-height column:
212	
213	```js
214	const NOGO = { x: -3, z: 4, r: 15, pad: 5 };   // padded box: x [-23,17], z [-16,24], all y
215	function inNoGo(x, z) {
216	  return x >= NOGO.x - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && x <= NOGO.x + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad
217	      && z >= NOGO.z - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && z <= NOGO.z + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad;
218	}
219	```
220	
221	Full-height column (not a y-slab): break-capable pathing under or over the
222	FEL base is foundation risk, not worth the shortcut.
223	
224	**Layer 2 — position watchdog.** `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` take no coords
225	and a legal `#goto` can still PATH THROUGH the zone (baritone cannot be told
226	to route around it). So the log-tail position parser doubles as watchdog:
227	parsed position inside the padded box → immediately `msg #stop`, then
228	`msg #goto <camp waypoint>`, mark task `aborted:nogo` in `/status`, log loud.
229	Watchdog is the backstop; the gate is the front door. Drivers should also
230	prefer targets whose straight line to the bot doesn't cross the box.
231

284	## Upstream status 2026-09-01
285	
286	Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
287	to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
288	forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform
289	in minecraft:blur/0" through "blur/5"; (2) hmc-specifics' JLine console
290	misbehaves when stdio is a plain pipe (no TTY), as the wrapper needs.
291	
292	### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms
293	
294	Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
295	uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
296	grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
297	`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
298	non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
299	bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
300	to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
301	and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
302	abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
303	(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
304	come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).
305	
306	Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
307	release:
308	- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
309	  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
310	  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
311	  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
312	  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
313	  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
314	  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
315	  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
316	- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
317	  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
318	  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
319	- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
320	  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
321	  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
322	- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
323	  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
324	- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
325	  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
326	  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
327	  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
328	  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
329	- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
330	  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
331	  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
332	  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.
333	
334	**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
335	own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
336	patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
337	More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
338	real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
339	over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
340	real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
341	gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
342	game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
343	redirection layer at all.
344	- hmc-specifics' console (`msg`, `connect`, `gui`, `click`) is confirmed to
345	  work identically with or without `-lwjgl` — see maintainer replies in
346	  [issue #230](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/230) and
347	  [issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390). Baritone
348	  chat-command control (part 3 of this doc) is unaffected by dropping the
349	  flag.
350	- Trade-off: a real (small, minimizable) game window per bot instance, and a
351	  sliver of real GPU/VRAM per client instead of zero. JVM heap budget in part
352	  6 is unaffected (that's CPU RAM, not GPU).
353	- If this stack ever moves to a true headless Linux box with no GPU at all,
354	  the Linux-native equivalent is Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe (software GL) in front
355	  of an un-patched launch — a working docker recipe is in
356	  [issue #249](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/249) (needs
357	  the `x11-xserver-utils` package per maintainer 3arthqu4ke, plus
358	  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Not directly usable on bare Windows (no X11);
359	  would need WSL2. Untested by this pass — field-verify separately if needed.
360	- If dropping `-lwjgl` is rejected and true headless is a hard requirement:
361	  this bucket is "fixable soon, not now" — file a new upstream issue with the
362	  exact blur/uniform log lines + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric. The
363	  maintainers (okafke, 3arthqu4ke) have a strong track record on this exact
364	  bug family — #388/#389 to merged fixes #406/#407 the same day.
365	
366	### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)
367	
368	Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
369	[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
370	"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
371	reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
372	reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
373	`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
374	section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").
375	
376	Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
377	`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
378	separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
379	guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
380	is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
381	that way.
382	
383	`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
384	one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
385	a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
386	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
387	  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
388	  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
389	- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
390	  version of the above.
391	
392	No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
393	ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
394	maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
395	reason to stand up a pty shim.
396	
397	**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
398	(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
399	from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.

422	### Verdict
423	
424	- **Blocker 1 (render hang): fixable now, not via any HMC flag/release, but
425	  via a launch-config change — drop `-lwjgl`, run BariBrute's client with a
426	  real (minimized) window on the real GPU.** This sidesteps HeadlessMc's
427	  incomplete RenderPipeline/uniform emulation, the near-certain cause, which
428	  is not fixed or even filed upstream for the blur pipeline specifically
429	  (2.9.0/2.10.0 only fixed the neighboring memSlice-NPE and 26.2 DeviceLimits
430	  gaps). If a fully invisible process is a hard requirement, this drops to
431	  "fixable soon" — file upstream and wait; track record is good but nothing
432	  to point to yet.
433	- **Blocker 2 (JLine over plain pipe): fixable now** via config property, no
434	  pty wrapper needed — `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first, else the
435	  confirmed `hmc.jline.enabled=false` from issue #390. Keep never using

# BARITONE-RUNNER.md — `baritone-runner.mjs` operator guide

HTTP wrapper around a real (headless-ish) Minecraft Java client driven by
Baritone, launched through HeadlessMc. One node process per bot, one HTTP port
per bot. Prototype bot: **BariBrute**, port **3301**.

Design blueprint lives in `cavecrew-mcp/cave/BARITONE.md`. This file is the
*operational* doc for the wrapper: how to run it, what the API is, how the
per-instance game directory works, what is pinned, and what it measured.

Status: **GREEN — end-to-end verified live 2026-09-01 08:20–08:24 local.**
Join, `/status`, `/goto` (two 20-block hops), `/stop`, `/disconnect`,
`/shutdown` all confirmed against the real `localhost:25565` server.

---

## 1. Launch

```powershell
cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter
node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 --host localhost --mcport 25565
```

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` | `BariBrute` | bot name; also the offline MC username, the `bots\<NAME>\` dir, and the pid file. Hard-capped at 16 chars (MC username limit) — the runner exits if longer. |
| `--port` | `3301` | HTTP control port, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Baritone heavy-lifters own 3301-3309. |
| `--host` | `localhost` | MC server host |
| `--mcport` | `25565` | MC server port |
| `--show-window` | off | leave the real GLFW window visible (debug only; default hides it) |

Boot timeline (all of it automatic):

```
t+0.0s   write bots/<NAME>/HeadlessMC/config.properties  (hmc.gamedir etc.)
t+0.0s   preflight: verify java, launcher jar, fabric version, pinned mods
t+0.0s   write <gamedir>/baritone/settings.txt  (safety block)
t+0.0s   delete stale <gamedir>/logs/latest.log, snapshot pre-existing java PIDs
t+0.0s   spawn  java -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar   (cwd = bots/<NAME>)
t+4.0s   stdin: launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"
t+39.0s  stdin: connect localhost 25565
t+51.0s  msg #set chatDebug true ; start position poll
```

Ready when `GET /status` returns `"phase":"in-world"` and a non-null
`position`. Typical wall time from launch to first position: **~55 s**.

### The three load-bearing quirks — do not "fix" them

1. **No `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's LWJGL redirection layer is incomplete for
   1.21.11's RenderPipeline, and the client hangs forever right after the
   `minecraft:blur/0` … `blur/5` uniform warnings. We run real LWJGL on the
   real GPU and hide the window instead.
2. **No `--quickPlayMultiplayer`.** It silently never fires on this HMC/MC
   pair — the client sits at the title screen forever with no log trace. The
   join is driven manually: after ~35 s, write `connect <host> <port>` to the
   launcher's stdin. (`hmc-specifics` `ConnectCommand` reads `args[1]` = host,
   `args[2]` = port; a raw space-separated line, no flags.)
3. **`-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false` on the CHILD JVM.** `hmc-specifics` mixes
   into `Minecraft.<init>` and starts a *second* JLine reader inside the game
