input.message:
Investigation done, no code touched. Found something concrete — worth reading before the rest.

(d) SERVER-SIDE CHECK, done first because it turned up gold: `datapack list` via RCON shows 6 datapacks, including **"ledger (Fabric mod)"**. Ledger is a real, known Fabric server mod (Rubydesic/Ledger, CoreProtect-equivalent for Fabric) — its whole job is logging every block change for admin rollback/inspection. Confirmed `/ledger` is a live command (RCON recognized the prefix, rejected bare `ledger`/`ledger help` as incomplete — real subcommand tree exists, needs `ledger search`/`ledger inspect`/`ledger rollback` etc.). I stopped guessing exact syntax through the RCON wrapper (kept hitting quoting issues indirectly) — you have direct console/RCON access and Ledger's own config/db, much faster for you to check than me blind-guessing subcommands. THIS is my top lead, not a coincidence I'd bet on: a mod that logs+can-rollback every block change, if its write is synchronous or contends under load, would produce EXACTLY this symptom (no error, no rollback trace on our side, block-update broadcast just doesn't arrive in time) — including explaining the vanished chest (a logging/rollback mod reverting a change without cleanly returning the item is a known bug class for this mod family).

(a) ALL confirmed coords, collected from FEEDBACK (your 3 + 2 more I found):
- (18,89,60) — Grog, roof-rim, 5/5 fail, neighbor (19,89,60) worked first try
- (11,86,55) — Thak, 20/20 fail, directly under chest A, correlated with a real movement-freeze right after
- (12,91,53) — Grog, north lamppost torch, 2/2 fail
- (7,104,31) — Bonk, trade-path, 2/2 fail (2 techniques), neighbor (7,106,31) worked first try
- (10,89,55) — Grog, double-chest: 1st attempt SUCCEEDED, then 8/8 fails on re-attempts, then item vanished entirely on attempt #10

(b) world-feature mapping: 4 of 5 are within ~10 blocks of camp/chest-A (10,89,55 is literally adjacent to chest A; 11,86,55 is directly under it; 12,91,53 is next to chest B; 18,89,60 is at the Mine House roof edge) — BUT (7,104,31) is ~25+ blocks from camp, near the trade-path, breaking a clean "camp-radius protection" theory on geography alone. Chunk-boundary check: only (7,104,31) sits on a chunk edge (z=31, local z=15) — weak, not a pattern across all 5.

(c) live read-only probes (UngaBunga, idle, /eval blockAt — no placements): 3 of 5 (18,89,60 / 11,86,55 / 7,104,31) are STILL air right now, matching their "worked around, left unfilled" history exactly. 2 of 5 (12,91,53 now cobblestone, 10,89,55 now oak_planks) have since been filled by something — worth asking whoever last touched those spots whether it eventually worked or someone built over/around it.

STATIC-CODE FINDING, rules one theory OUT cleanly: read mineflayer's own placeBlock/onceWithCleanup source (node_modules). The FEEDBACK authors' leading theory ("listener dedup keyed on coordinates, leaking across repeated attempts") is NOT what's happening — onceWithCleanup's listener removal is in a .finally(), fires on timeout AND success, confirmed no leak. The exact error text ("Event blockUpdate did not fire within timeout of 5000ms") is mineflayer's own hardcoded string, not ours, and the wait only triggers when the bot's OWN local block cache doesn't already show the change immediately after the place packet — meaning the block genuinely never got confirmed by the server within 5s, from our side we can't tell if the server silently rejected it or just never broadcast the confirm. Consistent with a server-side interceptor (Ledger) being in the loop.

VERDICT: hypothesis = Ledger mod's block-change logging (possibly synchronous DB write, possibly contending under bursty placement activity near camp where most of our traffic is) intermittently delays/drops the block-update broadcast past our 5s wait, independent of technique/ref/face — explains every symptom including the item loss. Not proven — needs your Ledger config/log access to confirm, that's the natural next step, not something I can do from here.

FIX/WORKAROUND (regardless of Ledger root cause): a curse-coordinate registry is the right pragmatic move — cheap, bounded, and helps immediately whether or not Ledger turns out to be the cause. Sketch: a small `cave/curse-coords.json` (or reuse zones.json's shape) that safePlaceBlock checks before attempting; a known-bad coordinate gets ONE extra retry with a longer wait (mineflayer's 5s is baked into placeBlock itself, not ours to extend directly — would need to catch-and-retry, which we already do once) then auto-offsets to an adjacent cell instead of hammering the same coordinate (matches what Grog/Bonk already did by hand both times). Population: manual for now (the 5 known coords), or auto-add after N fails at one spot in a session. Small, bounded — happy to build once files unlock, not attempting now per your investigation-only scope.

Nothing else touched. Ready for whatever's next.

input.message:
All 3 done, movement.js + skills.js only, committed. Report per fix:

**1. sealStairCell "no solid neighbor" (2/4 sides open)** — ROOT CAUSE: extendFloorTowards/sealStairCell/isSolidGround all checked `name==='air'` literal only. Dripstone caves read empty cells as `cave_air`/`void_air` — DIFFERENT block name. False-read as "already solid" -> floor-extend skipped placing, AND sealStairCell's own neighbor-search picked cave_air as a fake-solid ref, tried placing against it, failed, exhausted all directions. Proof this is a known pattern: `NOT_PLACED_RE` (cave_air|void_air|air|water|lava|bubble_column) already exists in this same file, already used correctly by placedAt()/pollPlaced — just never got ported to the seal chain. Swapped all 3 functions onto it.

**2. panic-eat "Item switched early to: undefined! Item: null" w/ 2 bread held** — WORSE bug than the wheat_seeds one, confirmed real via mineflayer-auto-eat source trace: it rejects the instant an inventory `updateSlot` fires for the food item's ORIGINAL `.slot` with newItem=null. `bestFood` was read ONCE outside the retry loop, reused BY REFERENCE across both attempts — stale slot snapshot, same "trust a reference not re-read state" bug class this codebase guards against everywhere else. Right after the 14-block placeBlock burst's own equip churn, the slot can still be settling when read, and attempt 1's own equip moves it again before a stale attempt-2 reuse. Fix: re-resolve findBestFoodItem() FRESH every attempt.

**3. Structural fall-guard** — added `attachFallGuard()` in movement.js, wired into goTo() via `ctx.isCancelled()` so BOTH engines' existing cancel plumbing (raceWithCancelAndTimeout poller for ash, retry-top check for pf) picks it up with ZERO changes inside gotoLoopPf/gotoAsh themselves. Trips on: cumulative drop >4 blocks since last onGround while velocity.y still falling, OR single-tick snap >3 blocks (catches Ook's exact "gap kept growing between checks" teleport-class shape even before velocity builds up) — used velocity as primary signal per your note. No opt-out param: grep-confirmed buildStaircase/branchMine never call goTo() at all (own hand-pulsed descent — advanceIntoStep already has its own runaway-fall guard, matches your "already has its own guard" call), so goTo() is plain-travel-only by construction, nothing to exempt.

2	// =============================================================================
3	// baritone-runner.mjs — HTTP wrapper around a HeadlessMc + Baritone MC client.
4	//
5	// One node process per bot. Command wire = HMC launcher stdin.
6	// State wire  = the game client's own <gameDir>/logs/latest.log tail.
7	// NO RCON anywhere in this file. LAW.
8	//
9	// Launch recipe below is the FIELD-PROVEN one from cave/BARITONE.md
10	// ("Round 2 FINAL update — verdict: WORKS", 2026-09-01) as first proven by
11	// hmc-launch8.mjs. Do not "improve" the three load-bearing quirks:
12	//   1. NO  -lwjgl               -> the headless render stub hangs forever on
13	//                                  1.21.11 blur-pipeline uniforms. Real GPU +
14	//                                  hidden real window instead.
15	//   2. NO  --quickPlayMultiplayer -> silently never fires on this HMC/MC pair.
16	//                                  Join is driven manually by writing
17	//                                  `connect <host> <port>` to launcher stdin
18	//                                  once the title screen is up (~35 s).
19	//   3. YES -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false -> hmc-specifics spins a SECOND JLine
20	//                                  reader inside Minecraft.<init>; over a
21	//                                  plain (non-TTY) pipe it throws
22	//                                  IllegalStateException and kills the client.
23	//                                  The softer hmc.jline.dumb.* flags do NOT
24	//                                  fix this one.
25	// =============================================================================
26	//
27	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	// PINNED VERSIONS  — every artifact below is an explicit, on-disk, pinned file.
29	//                    NOTHING in this runner resolves a "latest" URL or tag.
30	//                    The runner never downloads: preflight() fails loudly if a
31	//                    pinned file is missing rather than fetching a replacement.
32	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	//   Java runtime      : 21.0.10   C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe
34	//   HeadlessMc launcher: 2.10.0   bots/<NAME>/headlessmc-launcher.jar
35	//                                 (sha-identical copy of
36	//                                  shared/headlessmc-launcher.jar)
37	//   Minecraft         : 1.21.11
38	//   Fabric loader     : 0.19.3    version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`
39	//                                 installed under the SHARED mc install
40	//                                 (%APPDATA%\.minecraft\versions\...)
41	//   Fabric API mod    : 0.141.6+1.21.11
42	//                                 fabric-api-0.141.6+1.21.11.jar
43	//   Baritone          : 1.17.0    baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
44	//                                 (cabaletta official, built FOR 1.21.11)
45	//   hmc-specifics     : 2.4.0     hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar
46	//                                 (the version-stamped file HMC itself cached
47	//                                  under HeadlessMC/specifics/ — NOT the
48	//                                  "-latest" named download in shared/, which
49	//                                  would double-load as a second copy of the
50	//                                  same mod and crash fabric)
51	//
52	//   HMC_LAUNCH_TARGET below is the launcher's version selector. It is matched
53	//   against the installed version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`, which is
54	//   the only fabric version installed — so it is unambiguous, not a "latest".
55	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	//
57	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	// PER-INSTANCE gameDir — how two bots are kept from colliding
59	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	// HeadlessMc 2.10.0 ignores the launcher process cwd when choosing the game
61	// directory: by default it passes `--gameDir %APPDATA%\.minecraft` to every
62	// client it spawns. Two bots would then share one logs/latest.log (the state
63	// wire), one baritone/settings.txt, one options.txt, one servers.dat.
64	//
65	// Mechanism found (by decompiling headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar):
66	//   LauncherProperties.GAME_DIR = config key `hmc.gamedir`
67	//     -> LauncherBuilder reads it, defaulting to the mc install dir, and
68	//        FileManager.mkdir()s it
69	//     -> ProcessFactory passes it to the child JVM as `--gameDir <path>`
70	//        and logs `Game will run in <path>` (our proof line).
71	//   Sibling key `hmc.game.dir.for.each.version` would append a per-version
72	//   subdir; pinned to false so the path is exactly what we set.
73	//
74	// It is a CONFIG-FILE key, not a `launch` flag (the launch command has no
75	// gamedir flag), and HMC's config.properties is resolved from the launcher's
76	// cwd — which IS per bot. So the isolation is:
77	//
78	//   bots/<NAME>/                        <- launcher cwd, per bot
79	//     headlessmc-launcher.jar
80	//     HeadlessMC/config.properties      <- carries hmc.gamedir + offline user
81	//     HeadlessMC/<uuid>/                <- per-bot extracted natives (already
82	//                                          isolated by cwd, HMC-side)
83	//     gamedir/                          <- hmc.gamedir target, per bot
84	//       mods/                           <- pinned mods, per bot
85	//       logs/latest.log                 <- STATE WIRE, per bot
86	//       baritone/settings.txt           <- safety config, per bot
87	//       options.txt, servers.dat, saves/, screenshots/ ...
88	//
89	// Shared (read-mostly, safe to share, big): the mc install at
90	// %APPDATA%\.minecraft — versions/, libraries/, assets/. Those are content-
91	// addressed downloads, not per-session state, so sharing them costs nothing
92	// and saves ~1 GB per extra bot.
93	//
94	// writeHmcConfig() rewrites config.properties on every boot, so hmc.gamedir
95	// can never drift back to the shared profile.
96	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
